mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of quarters where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of periods where UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings visibility and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of three consecutive monthly INDPRO declines exceeding 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary shock, which increases real discount rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances where both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based weakening in demand drivers, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both fall > 1% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero (t-test p > 0.10) during periods where both PAYEMS and HOUST decline by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the labor force participation rate (implied by stable UNRATE but rising PAYEMS) above 62% for four consecutive months signals improved labor market tightness, which boosts wage pressures and ultimately supports higher corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE stable and PAYEMS rising while LFPR > 62% for 4 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of sustained labor force participation above 62% with stable unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS rising above its 5-year moving average for six consecutive months) signals elevated precautionary behavior by households, which reduces near-term consumption and corporate revenue, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of episodes where RSAFS exceeds its 5-year moving average for six consecutive months.
